# Environment of the API. Export these variables (or set them in your IDE) before running it. Never commit real values.

# Port the API listens on
PORT=8080

# Database connection (JDBC)

DATABASE_USER=api

files.README.md:
# catalog-api

REST API generated by [Model2API](https://raulesteveza.github.io/tools/Model2API/) with Ktor. It is a starting point: review it before using it in production.

## Run it

Requires Java 21 and Gradle 9 (or a Gradle wrapper: `gradle wrapper` creates one).

```bash
gradle run
```

Set the variables of `.env.example` in your environment first. The API listens on http://localhost:8080. Its contract is in `openapi.yaml`.

## Test it

```bash
gradle test
```

Each test starts the application anew, so it starts with empty storage.
The tests use a new in-memory H2 database for each test, or the mariadb database in `TEST_DATABASE_URL` (with `TEST_DATABASE_USER` and `TEST_DATABASE_PASSWORD`; its tables are dropped before each test).

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | What it does | Success | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/categories` | List categories | 200 | authenticated |
| `GET` | `/categories/{id}` | Get a category | 200 | authenticated |
| `POST` | `/categories` | Create a category | 201 | authenticated |
| `PUT` | `/categories/{id}` | Replace a category | 200 | authenticated |
| `PATCH` | `/categories/{id}` | Update part of a category | 200 | authenticated |
| `DELETE` | `/categories/{id}` | Delete a category | 204 | authenticated |
| `GET` | `/items` | List items | 200 | authenticated |
| `GET` | `/items/{id}` | Get an item | 200 | authenticated |
| `POST` | `/items` | Create an item | 201 | authenticated |
| `PUT` | `/items/{id}` | Replace an item | 200 | authenticated |
| `PATCH` | `/items/{id}` | Update part of an item | 200 | authenticated |
| `DELETE` | `/items/{id}` | Delete an item | 204 | authenticated |

Errors always have the same body: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "details": [...]}}`. Invalid requests answer 400.

## Storage

Exposed on mariadb. The application creates the tables that are missing when it starts, while you develop; for a real database, use migrations (Model2DB writes them). Embedded objects and lists are stored as JSON text, and references as key columns.

## Authentication

Protected endpoints need a key in the `X-API-Key` header, one of the comma-separated keys in `API_KEYS`. Without `API_KEYS`, every protected request is rejected.

## Structure

```text
src/main/kotlin/com/example/api/
  Application.kt        entry point: wires storage, services and routes
  common/               errors, request bodies, JSON, lists and settings
  model/                domain classes, enums and embedded objects
  dto/                  request bodies and responses
  repository/           storage
  service/              rules of each resource
  routes/               HTTP routes
  database/             connection and tables
  security/             authentication
src/test/kotlin/         one test class per resource
openapi.yaml             the contract of the API
```

## Left to you

- Nothing marked: review the generated code before using it.

package com.example.api

import com.example.api.common.JsonFormat
import com.example.api.common.Settings
import com.example.api.common.installErrors
import com.example.api.database.connectDatabase
import com.example.api.repository.ExposedCategoryRepository
import com.example.api.repository.ExposedItemRepository
import com.example.api.routes.categoryRoutes
import com.example.api.routes.itemRoutes
import com.example.api.security.installSecurity
import com.example.api.service.CategoryService
import com.example.api.service.ItemService
import io.ktor.serialization.kotlinx.json.json
import io.ktor.server.application.Application
import io.ktor.server.application.ApplicationStopped
import io.ktor.server.application.install
import io.ktor.server.engine.embeddedServer
import io.ktor.server.netty.Netty
import io.ktor.server.plugins.contentnegotiation.ContentNegotiation
import io.ktor.server.routing.routing

/** Starts the API on PORT (8080 by default) with the settings of the environment. */
fun main() {
    val port = System.getenv("PORT")?.toIntOrNull() ?: 8080
    embeddedServer(Netty, port = port) { module(Settings.fromEnvironment()) }.start(wait = true)
}

/** The API: JSON, errors, authentication, storage and routes. */
fun Application.module(settings: Settings) {
    install(ContentNegotiation) { json(JsonFormat) }
    installErrors()
    installSecurity(settings)

    // Each repository keeps its items in the database with Exposed
    val database = connectDatabase(settings)
    monitor.subscribe(ApplicationStopped) { database.close() }
    val categoryRepository = ExposedCategoryRepository(database.database)
    val itemRepository = ExposedItemRepository(database.database)
    val categoryService = CategoryService(categoryRepository)
    val itemService = ItemService(itemRepository, categoryRepository)

    routing {
        categoryRoutes(categoryService)
        itemRoutes(itemService)
    }
}

package com.example.api.dto

import com.example.api.common.Checks
import com.example.api.common.JsonDecimal
import com.example.api.common.JsonKind
import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable
import kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonObject

/** Body of a request that creates or replaces an item. */
@Serializable
data class ItemCreate(
    val name: String? = null,
    val price: JsonDecimal? = null,
    val supplierEmail: String? = null,
    val categoryId: Long? = null,
    val stock: Int? = null,
) {
    companion object {
        /** What the body must meet, checked on its JSON before it is read. */
        fun rules(checks: Checks, json: JsonObject) {
            checks.required(json, "name")
            checks.notNull(json, "name")
            checks.kind(json, "name", JsonKind.TEXT)
            checks.length(json, "name", 3, 120)
            checks.required(json, "price")
            checks.notNull(json, "price")
            checks.kind(json, "price", JsonKind.NUMBER)
            checks.range(json, "price", "0", null, false, false)
            checks.required(json, "supplierEmail")
            checks.notNull(json, "supplierEmail")
            checks.kind(json, "supplierEmail", JsonKind.TEXT)
            checks.email(json, "supplierEmail")
            checks.required(json, "categoryId")
            checks.notNull(json, "categoryId")
            checks.kind(json, "categoryId", JsonKind.WHOLE)
            checks.required(json, "stock")
            checks.notNull(json, "stock")
            checks.kind(json, "stock", JsonKind.WHOLE)
            checks.range(json, "stock", "0", null, false, false)
        }
    }
}

            checks.range(json, "price", "0", null, false, false)
            checks.notNull(json, "supplierEmail")
